title: Ranveer Singh Has Acquired the Rights to The Immortals of Meluha. He Will Play Lord Shiva. It Is One of Three Films He Is Building Simultaneously.
excerpt: A zombie thriller, a mythological trilogy, and a Dhurandhar director reunion. The post-Dhurandhar empire is taking shape, and its ambition is unprecedented.
body:
Ranveer Singh has acquired the film rights to Amish Tripathi's bestselling novel *The Immortals of Meluha* under his production banner Maa Kasam Films. He will play Lord Shiva in what is being developed as a grand-scale cinematic trilogy in partnership with Birla Studios. The first part is expected to go on floors in 2028.

This is not a standalone announcement. It is the third major project Ranveer has stacked in his pipeline since the Dhurandhar duology crossed ₹3,100 crore worldwide — a franchise return that has fundamentally altered his position in the industry.

## The Three Bets

**Pralay** is the most immediate. A post-apocalyptic zombie thriller directed by Jai Mehta (of *Scam 1992* fame), it is mounted on a ₹300 crore budget and is scheduled to begin shooting in August 2026. The film is produced by Hansal Mehta's True Story Films and Ranveer's own Maa Kasam Films. Kalyani Priyadarshan makes her Hindi debut opposite Ranveer. The tone, per reports, sits somewhere between *World War Z* and *I Am Legend* — a survival story about a man fighting to save his family.

**The Immortals of Meluha** is the long game. Amish Tripathi's 2010 novel reimagines Lord Shiva as a human hero whose journey transforms him into a divine figure. The book sold over five million copies and spawned a trilogy that became a cultural phenomenon among urban Indian readers. The adaptation is currently in the screenplay stage, with the director yet to be locked. If it reaches production, it could become one of the biggest franchise attempts in Indian cinema history.

**An untitled project with Aditya Dhar** — the director of both Dhurandhar films — is reportedly expected to start shooting in March 2027. No details have been revealed, but the director-actor pairing now carries a commercial guarantee that few combinations in Bollywood can match.

## What Changed After Dhurandhar

The Dhurandhar duology did not just make money. It made Ranveer Singh the most bankable actor in Indian cinema by a significant margin. The combined worldwide gross of ₹3,107 crore across both films, produced on a combined budget of just ₹255 crore, represents a return on investment that the industry had never seen at this scale. The digital rights alone — ₹85 crore to Netflix for Part 1, ₹150 crore to JioHotstar for Part 2 — nearly covered the entire production cost.

This financial leverage is what allows Ranveer to simultaneously pursue a ₹300 crore zombie thriller, a mythological trilogy, and a reunion with his most successful director. Two years ago, any one of these projects would have been considered a major risk. Now they are parallel bets backed by proof.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRI audiences, two of these three projects carry immediate resonance. *The Immortals of Meluha* is widely read in diaspora book clubs and has been a staple recommendation in Indian communities abroad since its release. A big-budget adaptation starring Ranveer Singh could drive the kind of cultural-event moviegoing that Bollywood has struggled to create outside of the top five franchises. *Pralay*, meanwhile, enters a genre — the zombie apocalypse — that has massive global audiences but has never been attempted at this scale by an Indian production. If the quality matches the ambition, it could be the rare Indian film that doesn't need a diaspora hook to find international audiences.

## The Risk

None of this is guaranteed. Indian cinema is littered with ambitious announcements that never reached production. The Meluha rights have changed hands before. And a ₹300 crore zombie film from the director of a web series — however acclaimed — is the kind of bet that can go spectacularly wrong. But the Dhurandhar machine has given Ranveer something few actors in any film industry get: the capital, the credibility, and the runway to swing for the fences on three projects simultaneously.
